speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. To better assess the newborn's jaundice, when did the yellow discoloration first appear, and how old is the infant in days?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-week-old female newborn. The patient has been experiencing increasing yellow discoloration of her eyes and skin for 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation, initially weighed 3066 g and now weighs 3200 g. The patient is exclusively breastfed.

speaker: Doctor
text: I note the infant is gaining weight well and is exclusively breastfed, which are positive signs. To rule out pathology, are the stools pale or clay-colored, and is the urine dark yellow or tea-colored?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Increasing yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin. I also have Exclusively breastfed, Brother died 3 months after liver surgery.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your brother's history of liver surgery and death, I am concerned about a genetic condition like Galactosemia. Has the baby developed any vomiting, poor feeding, or an enlarged liver or spleen? REQUEST TEST: Serum Galactose-1-phosphate uridyltransferase activity

speaker: Doctor
text: Since galactosemia is ruled out, the normal weight gain and exclusive breastfeeding point toward Breast Milk Jaundice, which typically presents after the first week of life. I will check the bilirubin levels to confirm this benign condition. REQUEST TEST: Total and Direct Serum Bilirubin

speaker: Doctor
text: The bilirubin levels indicate unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia, which is consistent with breast milk jaundice in a well-hydrated, weight-gaining infant. DIAGNOSIS READY: Breast Milk Jaundice
